title: Purpose of the issues practice
blurb: Explain what the issues practice is for, what counts as an issue, and why it now includes change control.
question: A supplier confirms that a delivery has already slipped, and the senior user wants an extra feature added to an approved design. Which practice handles both, and why?

teach.body: Formally, the purpose of the issues practice is to collect and assess issues and control changes to the project's baseline. In plain English: whenever something happens that the project management team needs to think about, or someone wants to alter a product that has already been approved, the issues practice makes sure it is recorded, its impact is understood and the right person decides what to do.

An issue is an event relevant to the project that requires project management consideration. Anyone with an interest in the project can raise one, at any time. Issues can be bad news (a problem), good news (a business opportunity) or a proposal (a request for change). The test is relevance: an event that needs a response from the wider business, and does not touch the project, is not a project issue.

children.label: Not a project issue

teach.body: In PRINCE2 7, issue management encompasses change control. A change is a modification to any approved product in the project baseline, and the project baseline is the current approved versions of the management and project products that are subject to change control. So the same practice that captures problems also decides whether a baselined product may be altered.

head: 6th edition (2017)
PRINCE2 7

teach.caption: Older study material that talks about the 'change theme' is describing what is now the issues practice.

teach.body: Fenmoor District Council is replacing its paper parking permits with a digital service. Project manager Priya Nair hears from the supplier that the permit database licence has already been delayed by two weeks: that is an issue, not a risk, because it has happened. The same week, senior user Tom Ashby asks to add visitor permits to the approved product description: a request for change. Priya captures both in the issue register and assesses their impact before anything is decided.

teach.text: Two classic traps. First, something that has already happened is an issue, not a risk, even if it was once on the risk register. Second, change control (issues practice) is NOT change management: change management is the people element's work of moving the organization to its target state.

items: Purpose: collect and assess issues and control changes to the project's baseline.
Issue: an event relevant to the project that requires project management consideration; anyone can raise one at any time.
Issues can be negative, positive or a proposal for change.
In PRINCE2 7, issue management encompasses change control (the old change theme).
An event needing a response from the business, not the project, is not a project issue.

summary: You can now state the purpose of the issues practice: to collect and assess issues and control changes to the project's baseline. You can also tell an issue from a risk and explain why PRINCE2 7 places change control inside issue management.

A.q: What is the purpose of the issues practice?
options: To identify, assess and control uncertainties that would affect objectives
To monitor and compare actual achievements against those that were planned
To collect and assess issues and control changes to the project's baseline
To document the user's requirements and establish how they will be met
A.why: The issues practice collects and assesses issues and controls changes to the project's baseline (manual 10.1).

whyNot.0: That is the purpose of the risk practice.
whyNot.3: That is the purpose of the quality practice.

A.q: A new team member asks what PRINCE2 7 means by an 'issue'. Which description is correct?
options: An event relevant to the project that requires project management consideration
An uncertain event that, should it occur, would affect the project's objectives
A modification to an approved product that forms part of the project baseline
A forecast that a stage or the whole project will move outside its tolerances
A.why: An issue is an event relevant to the project that requires project management consideration (manual 10.1).

whyNot.1: That is the definition of a risk.
whyNot.2: That is the definition of a change.
whyNot.3: That describes an exception, which is reported in an exception report.

A.q: Identify the missing word in the following sentence. In PRINCE2 7, issue management encompasses [?] control.
options: quality
progress
cost
change
A.why: PRINCE2 7 states that issue management encompasses change control, which was the old change theme.

whyNot.0: Quality control belongs to the quality practice.
whyNot.1: Progress control belongs to the progress practice.
whyNot.2: Cost is one of the seven performance aspects controlled through tolerances, not what issue management encompasses.

B.q:
Which two statements about issues are correct?
1. An issue can be raised by anyone with an interest in the project, at any time.
2. An event that has already happened and affects the project is an issue rather than a risk.
3. The issues practice plans how users will move from the current state to the target state.
4. An issue must have a negative impact on the project.
options: 1 and 2
1 and 3
2 and 4
3 and 4
B.why: Anyone can raise an issue at any time (1), and an event that has already happened is an issue, not a risk (2).

whyNot.1: Statement 3 is false: moving people to the target state is change management, part of the people element.
whyNot.2: Statement 4 is false: a business opportunity is an issue with positive consequences.
whyNot.3: Both are false: transition is change management, and issues can be positive.

B.q: A supplier confirms that a key component has already been dispatched three weeks late. Which practice should handle this?
options: The risk practice
The issues practice
The quality practice
The plans practice
B.why: The delay has already happened, so it is an issue to be captured and assessed in the issues practice.

whyNot.0: The risk practice handles uncertain future events; this delay is already certain.
whyNot.2: The quality practice covers quality specifications and checks, not a late delivery.
whyNot.3: Plans may later be updated, but the event itself is captured and assessed as an issue.

B.q: Which statement about the issues practice in PRINCE2 7 is correct?
options: It replaced the 6th edition risk theme
It is the new home of change management
It is part of the people element
It replaced the 6th edition change theme
B.why: The 6th edition change theme became the issues practice, and issue management now encompasses change control.

whyNot.0: The risk theme became the risk practice.
whyNot.1: Change management (organizational transition) belongs to the people element, not the issues practice.
whyNot.2: The issues practice is one of the seven practices; it is not part of the people element.

C.q: A housing directorate faces a staff shortage that its own managers must respond to. The project team has checked that it does not affect any project product, plan or the business case. How should the project treat it?
options: As a request for change, entered in the issue register
As a threat, entered in the risk register for monitoring
As a concern, assessed by the project manager for impact
As outside the project, needing no project consideration
C.why: An issue must be relevant to the project and need project management consideration. An event that needs a response from the business, with no effect on the project, is not a project issue.

whyNot.0: A request for change proposes a change to a baseline; nothing in the project is to be changed here.
whyNot.1: The shortage is not an uncertain event affecting project objectives; it has happened and does not touch the project.
whyNot.2: Its impact has already been assessed and found to be nil, so there is nothing further for the project to consider.

C.q: Which pair shows BOTH what the issues practice collects AND what it controls?
options: Issues; changes to the project baseline
Risks; changes to the project baseline
Issues; movement to the target state
Lessons; deviations from stage plans
C.why: The practice collects and assesses issues and controls changes to the project's baseline (manual 10.1).

whyNot.1: Risks are collected by the risk practice.
whyNot.2: Movement to the target state is change management in the people element.
whyNot.3: Lessons are captured through progress, and deviations from plans are controlled in the progress practice.

C.q: Which statement about raising issues is correct?
options: Issues are raised by the project manager at each stage boundary
Issues are raised by the business layer before initiation begins
Anyone may raise an issue at any time during the project
Issues are raised by project assurance after each quality review
C.why: An issue can be raised by anyone with an interest in the project, at any time, through formal or informal channels.

whyNot.0: Issues are captured throughout the stage, not held back until a stage boundary.
whyNot.1: The business layer provides the mandate; issues arise and are captured throughout the project.
whyNot.3: Project assurance advises the board; issues are not limited to assurance or to quality reviews.

reteach.title: The kitchen refit
reteach.question: During a kitchen refit, which events need the builder's attention, and which are someone else's business?

blocks.body: A good builder keeps a notebook of everything that needs a decision: the worktop arriving cracked (a problem), the owner asking for an extra socket (a request for change), a cheaper sink becoming available (a business opportunity). A rumour that the tiles might be discontinued next year is a risk, not yet an issue. The neighbour's own extension is not the builder's business at all. That notebook, plus the rule that nobody alters the agreed design without approval, is the issues practice.

blocks.text: If it has already happened and the project must consider it, it is an issue. If it is uncertain, it is a risk. If it needs no project consideration, it is not a project issue.

explain.body: The issues practice has two jobs: collect and assess issues, and control changes to the project's baseline. In PRINCE2 7 these sit together because issue management encompasses change control.

test.q: Which practice controls changes to the project's baseline?
options: The quality practice
The plans practice
The progress practice
The issues practice
test.why: Controlling changes to the project's baseline is part of the purpose of the issues practice.

whyNot.0: The quality practice defines requirements and checks products against them.
whyNot.1: The plans practice creates the plans; changes to approved plans go through the issues practice.
whyNot.2: The progress practice monitors and controls deviations from plans.

explain.body: A risk is uncertain; an issue has happened or is certain. A register entry that describes something already true is really an issue, or the cause of a risk, not a risk.

test.q: A risk register entry reads: 'The site access road has flooded and deliveries have stopped.' Why is this entry wrong?
options: It describes something that has happened, so it is an issue
It has no named risk owner, so it belongs in the daily log
It affects time, so it belongs in the stage plan instead
It affects cost, so it belongs in the business case instead
test.why: A current state of affairs is an issue, not a risk, so it should be captured through the issues practice.

whyNot.1: A missing owner is not the problem; the event has already happened, which makes it an issue.
whyNot.2: The stage plan may be updated later, but the event is captured as an issue first.
whyNot.3: Any effect on the business case is assessed as part of handling the issue.

explain.body: The project baseline is the current approved versions of the management and project products that are subject to change control. A change is a modification to any of them.

options: The first version of the PID, approved at the end of initiation
The set of tolerances the board has agreed for the current stage
The current approved versions of products under change control
The list of all products required by a plan, with their status
test.why: The project baseline is the current approved versions of the management products and project products that are subject to change control (manual 10.1).

whyNot.0: The baseline is the current approved versions, which change as approved changes are made; it is not frozen at the first PID.
whyNot.1: Stage tolerances are limits of delegated authority, not the baseline.

explain.body: Ask: has it happened, and does the project need to consider it? A failed product, a supplier delay or a proposal to alter an approved product all qualify. A possible future event is a risk; a lesson is recorded in the lessons log.

root.label: Happened and relevant to the project?

test.q: Which situation is a project issue?
options: A threat that a supplier might go out of business next year
A tester finds a delivered product fails its quality specification
A department must respond to a new law that does not touch the project
A lesson from an earlier project about writing supplier contracts
test.why: A product that will not meet its quality specification is an off-specification, a type of issue.

whyNot.0: A possible future failure is a risk, not an issue.
whyNot.2: An event needing a response from the business, not the project, is not a project issue.
whyNot.3: A lesson is recorded in the lessons log, not as an issue.
